name: Acoustic Cavity Resonance Pistol ACRP-2 'Hollowpoint'
description:
The ACRP-2 fires a tightly focused beam of low-frequency acoustic energy calibrated to resonate within enclosed anatomical spaces — specifically the thoracic cavity, cranial vault, and sinus structures. Unlike broad-spectrum sonic weapons that rely on general pressure waves, the Hollowpoint uses a target-specific frequency-mapping pre-fire scan lasting approximately 0.3 seconds to calculate the resonant frequency of the target's body cavities based on their approximate mass and build. The resulting beam then drives those cavities into constructive resonance, producing internal pressure oscillations that rupture soft tissue and, at close range, fracture bone without any external impact signature.

The weapon's beam is completely invisible and nearly silent — it produces a faint low hum audible only to the operator. Victims experience the effects as sudden, catastrophic internal failure: hemorrhage, disorientation, loss of motor control, and in high-power mode, cardiac disruption from resonance interference with the heart's mechanical rhythm. At distances beyond fifteen meters, the beam disperses enough that effects are reduced to severe nausea, disorientation, and incapacitation rather than lethal cavity rupture.

Tessera Corponation's research division developed the ACRP-2 under a classified contract before spinning the technology into a commercial chassis. The scanning and targeting system — originally designed for non-destructive structural testing in construction applications — was repurposed with minimal modification, a fact that Tessera's legal team has worked hard to keep out of public record. The weapon leaves no ballistic signature, no chemical trace, and causes injuries that can be initially mistaken for spontaneous medical events, making it extraordinarily difficult to attribute in forensic investigations.
specifications:
effective range lethal: 0–15 meters
effective range incapacitating: 15–40 meters
pre-fire scan duration: 0.3 seconds
beam width at 10m: 12cm diameter
power modes: Low (incapacitation), High (lethal)
magazine capacity: 22 charges (ultrasonic power cell)
weight: 1.1 kg
dimensions: 24cm x 12cm x 4cm
audible signature: Sub-60dB operator-side hum only
tactical_use: The ACRP-2 is a precision assassination tool used in environments where conventional weapons would be detected or traced. Operators exploit its lack of visible or audible signature to eliminate targets in semi-public spaces — the victim appears to suffer a sudden medical collapse. The 0.3-second scan delay requires a momentary stable aim, which limits its use in fast-moving close-quarters engagements. Experienced operators pre-scan targets before entering a room using the weapon's passive mode, then activate on demand with no additional delay. In low-power mode, the weapon is used to silently disable targets who are then rendered unconscious and removed from scene.
cultural_context: Among GLMZ's criminal and corporate assassination ecology, the Hollowpoint occupies a rarefied position — it is a weapon for people who are paid to make deaths look like accidents. Its existence is not widely known outside specialist circles, and even within those circles it is discussed obliquely. The few operators who carry it rarely advertise the fact; the weapon's value is entirely dependent on its obscurity. There is a persistent urban legend that the weapon was used in at least two 'natural causes' deaths of prominent figures in GLMZ — a rumor that Tessera Corponation vigorously and consistently denies.
known_users: Mireille Fontaine-Cross (alleged — linked to four unexplained executive deaths)
Certain GLMZ intelligence service field operatives (officially denied)
story_hooks: A powerful figure dies of apparent cardiac arrest in a crowded public event. The players are the only ones who notice the faint hum — and now they know something they weren't supposed to.
A stolen ACRP-2 is being auctioned on the black market, drawing bidders from three different factions simultaneously. The players are hired by one — but the others know they're coming.
A forensic investigator has quietly compiled evidence linking the Hollowpoint to six deaths ruled as natural causes. She needs protection while she figures out who to trust with the information.
A player character's contact dies suddenly in front of them — no wound, no weapon, no trace. The only lead is a faint structural resonance reading on their augmented hearing implant.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist pistol that resembles a precision medical diagnostic tool more than a lethal weapon. The profile is angular and geometric, with a pronounced forward-swept transducer array forming a subtle bulge at the muzzle. The overall aesthetic is clinical and corporate — nothing about it suggests weaponry to untrained eyes.
physical_description.dimensions: 240mm length, 120mm height, 40mm depth. The muzzle transducer cluster extends 35mm beyond the frame.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light in hand — approximately 1.1kg distributed across a compact frame gives it an almost toy-like feel despite its lethal function. The balance tilts slightly forward due to the transducer array, requiring deliberate control.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite over a titanium-reinforced internal structure. The frame is a matte graphite composite designed to absorb thermal signature.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with subtle surface texture to reduce reflection. The transducer array housing features a darker charcoal anodized finish with micro-etched grip panels.
physical_description.color_scheme: Monochromatic gray-to-black gradient: matte graphite body with charcoal accents at the muzzle and trigger guard. Minimal chrome on internal springs visible through the ejection port.
physical_description.grip_texture: Micro-textured polymer with embedded grip grooves, designed for precision two-finger indexing. The surface is slightly tacky, non-reflective, and engineered to absorb moisture without becoming slick.
distinctive_features: Forward-mounted piezoelectric transducer array: 7 hexagonal projectors arranged in a compact cluster, faintly visible through the translucent cowl
Minimal iron sights: low-profile tritium dots integrated into the slide
Passive scan indicator: subtle LED in the grip that pulses faintly when pre-scan mode is active
Ultrasonic power cell port: located on the left side, recessed flush with the frame
No visible trigger guard articulation — the trigger itself retracts fully when not in firing position
Dissipation vents: three thin parallel slots along the left side of the barrel for piezo heat management
Serial port hidden under a flush-fit maintenance panel at the grip heel
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Seo Research Compliance Group logo (stylized Φ symbol in a circle) stamped discretely on the grip panel in matte silver. Serial number laser-etched on the right side of the frame in 6mm characters. No model designation visible on the exterior — all branding is minimal and corporate.
physical_description.condition_typical: Immaculate. The ACRP-2 is a precision tool maintained obsessively by its operators. Field examples show virtually no wear: no scuff marks, no powder residue (none exists), no mechanical degradation. When neglected, dust accumulation on the transducer cowl is the only sign of use.
